Command: Priests shall eat the flesh of the firstborn animals
Summary: The command: Priests shall eat the flesh of the firstborn animals (Numbers 18:18). The priests ate the flesh of the firstborn in the holy place, as part of their appointed portion.
Commandment: Priests shall eat the flesh of the firstborn animals, as prescribed in Numbers 18:18.
Application: It cannot be practised as written without the standing temple and Aaronic priesthood; its enduring lesson is God's holiness, the cost of atonement, and worship offered exactly as God appoints.
Purpose: Scripture's stated ground: the firstborn's flesh belonged to the priests as their appointed portion (Numbers 18:18).
Function: The priests ate the flesh of the firstborn in the holy place, as part of their appointed portion — a ceremonial law of priestly eating. Its goal was to sustain Aaron's house from the firstborn offerings, the flesh that belonged to the LORD feeding the men who served him. It did not address a particular evil; its work was provision and remembrance, not restraint. The firstborn that remembered Egypt fed the priesthood, and the memory and the meal were one.
